transfer.staging.optDetailsSummary: What "Optimize" does · why the master copy is always kept
transfer.staging.optNote: Clicking "Optimize" cleans + optimizes: strips font/size/color/alignment locks · zeroes margins/spacing and applies CJK/Latin-appropriate first-line indent · auto-builds a table of contents when missing · strips pseudo-DRM · inlines footnotes in place · inlines remote images · downsamples images · boosts e-ink contrast · dedupes duplicate ids. The master copy is always kept — so you can add the same book to the other reader for comparison, or re-add after switching devices; delete it yourself from the list once you don’t need it.

transfer.guide.summary: How does the master library work? Which reader should I pick? (click to expand)
transfer.guide.steps.dd: ① Intake: upload (book formats) / grab an article / scp into inbox — the book goes into the master library as-is, bytes untouched. ② Optimize (optional): for EPUB, click "Optimize" to clean up layout, footnotes, CJK/Latin indentation (PDF isn’t touched on-device). ③ Deliver: click "Add to xochitl" or "Add to KOReader". The master copy stays put, so you can add it to the other reader any time. The reader pages (xochitl / KOReader) only manage their own fonts and dictionaries, not book transfer.
transfer.guide.format.dd: Only {native} is accepted — regardless of whether the device could technically read other formats, only these two are taken; convert anything else yourself before uploading. The master library "Optimize" button optimizes EPUB in place; oversized comic EPUBs are automatically split into volumes for adding to xochitl, no separate CBZ conversion needed. PDF can be optimized too: PDFs with a text layer are converted to EPUB (images, formulas and a table of contents kept); scanned/comic PDFs without a text layer are only margin-trimmed, format unchanged.
transfer.guide.native.dt: 📖 Add to xochitl: books you’ll annotate
transfer.guide.native.dd: TOC navigation, footnotes, font switching, direct handwritten annotation, AI interpretation. Put academic papers or anything you'll highlight here; finalized handwritten-annotation PDFs go here too.
transfer.guide.koreader.dt: 📚 Add to KOReader: casual reading, dictionary lookups
transfer.guide.koreader.dd: Free reflow, built-in dictionary, page-turn gestures. Good for novels, comics, foreign-language books.
transfer.guide.unsure.dd: Add it to one. The master copy stays, so you can add it to the other any time for comparison — don’t overthink "casual vs. study", it’s your call (some read detective novels for fun, others use them to map out clues; some just read comics, others study the art).

notes.title: Notes
notes.lead: Highlight and jot notes in the margin, then close the book — new annotations land in "Browse" first: take a look, click "Send to notes" to transcribe it and move it to "Organize" for review, or "Not needed" to skip it for good. Model keys are configured on the "Manage" tab.

notes.trash.lead: This holds annotations skipped via "Not needed" / "Not needed anymore", plus entries auto-flagged after their strokes were erased — neither projection uses them anymore, but they stay in the entry store until you clear them by hand. Restoring puts an entry roughly back where it was (proofread text still there → back to "Proofread"; only a draft → back to "To proofread"; only handwriting, never transcribed → back to "To transcribe"; nothing left at all → back to "Browse" to decide again).
notes.trash.purgeTitle: Permanently remove the entries listed below — cannot be undone
notes.import.lead: An independent path from "Browse/Organize" above: skips the entry store entirely and turns one .md file directly into a new device notebook document, placed in the currently selected book's own device folder. Headings/lists/todos become native xochitl styles; inline bold/italic only has its markup stripped, it doesn't render (typed styling applies to a whole paragraph, not half a sentence); checked todos can't be written as checked, they land unchecked.

battop.title: Battery Assassin (battop)
battop.toggle.desc: A sampling diagnostic process for tracking down battery drain — you won't need it day to day. It caused a cgroup deadlock/hang once in August 2026: the root cause is a rare kernel RCU stall (never fixed, a probability event); back then a timer restarting it every 10 minutes amplified the odds of hitting it 144x. It's since been changed to run continuously at a low sample rate, so a normal occasional start/stop click carries negligible risk — but every "start" still runs the same cgroup migration step, so clicking start/stop repeatedly in quick succession isn't absolutely safe; don't treat this toggle as a free button to mash. Turning it on adds a "Battery Assassin" second-level tab under "Manage" with detailed usage/wake-source data.
battop.toggle.label: Enable
battop.toggle.notInstalled: See enhance/battop/install.sh to install by hand (this page only controls an already-installed copy, it doesn't install from the web)
battop.noSamplesYet: No samples yet — the always-on service samples roughly every 10 minutes, give it one cycle right after installing/starting it.

manage.foundation.title: Setup · foundation
manage.foundation.lead: Shelf's features are built on top of xovi + appload. Use the desktop reManager (or vellum on the device) to get the foundation in place first — KOReader installs itself from its own official repo — then come back here to manage each shelf feature.
manage.foundation.links: Downloads / docs: reManager (desktop · vellum ecosystem) · xovi · KOReader Wiki
manage.modules.title: Shelf features
manage.modules.lead: Each feature can be toggled or uninstalled independently; a not-installed one only shows the install command. The gateway (this page) is always on.
manage.modules.helpSummary: What do the three states / toggle / uninstall / install mean? (click to expand)
manage.modules.help.states.dd:
Not installed nothing on the device yet → run the given command to install.
Installed · off present but not running in the background → the page can't show its features, click "Enable".
On running in the background → it has a tab up top and its features are usable.
manage.modules.help.toggle.dd: Disable only stops the background service: the page hides that tab, but what's already taken effect keeps working — an installed font is still selectable in the reader, a wallpaper still shows, KOReader still opens; you just can't push/change it from the web anymore. Useful for hiding features you don't use and shrinking the exposed surface.
manage.modules.help.perf.dt: Does leaving everything on lag or drain the battery?
manage.modules.help.perf.dd: No. Measured: all 5 services left on together use about 9 MB of memory and under 2 seconds of CPU across a full day (roughly 0.002% average) — they mostly sit blocked waiting for requests and never compete for CPU. Zero perceptible impact on reading or note-taking, no lag, no extra battery use. Recommended to leave everything on unless you're sure you'll never use a given feature.
manage.modules.help.uninstall.dd: Removes that feature's program, systemd unit, and any injected files (qmd). Books/fonts/wallpapers etc. you've already transferred are kept. After uninstalling it disappears from the page; reinstall with the install command to bring it back. The gateway itself can't be disabled or uninstalled from the web — it's the host of this Manage page.
manage.modules.help.install.dt: Why isn't installing done from the web?
manage.modules.help.install.dd: Installing needs to remount a read-only system partition and write system units — risk is higher. Not-installed features only get a command: run it over SSH from a computer, or go through reManager's guided setup instead, which is safer.
manage.modules.confirmUninstall: Uninstall {label}? Removes its service/unit/related qmd (user data is kept).
manage.modules.confirmAllOff: Disable every domain service (keep the gateway)?
manage.models.title: Models
manage.models.lead: Cloud models used by the notes line for transcribing annotations (vision model) and Ask AI (text model). Pick a preset combination — no need to fill in a service address yourself; a type with no key configured just won't be usable for its feature.
manage.enhance.hlSnap.title: CJK highlight snapping
manage.enhance.hlSnap.desc: Highlighting Chinese text snaps precisely to word/line boundaries instead of "highlight a bit, grab the whole line". The C hook inside langhook reads this toggle live and applies it immediately, no restart needed; the native "Settings" app's "System enhance" page has the same toggle — either side takes effect.
manage.lab.hwStroke.title: CJK handwriting stroke tuning
manage.lab.hwStroke.desc: Adjusts stroke thickness by pen direction/speed on the device (a nib-angle model plus a press-speed proxy, layered together) — unrelated to the "capture and transcribe" AI pipeline; this is about how the stroke itself is drawn. Currently only verified on real hardware for some pen types (calligraphy pen, marker-class tools) — the pen/pencil-weight tools used most day to day still can't be pinned down (virtual-function dynamic dispatch, the runtime target hasn't been identified yet — see enhance/handwriting-stroke/README.md "现状" (Status)). This toggle directly changes two intensity thresholds in reading-qol.json; the very next stroke picks it up, no xochitl restart needed.
manage.lab.importMd.title: Import md file
manage.lab.importMd.desc: Once enabled, an "Import md file" sub-tab appears on the "Notes" tab (upload a .md file to generate a device notebook document). New feature, off by default — turn it on here to use it.
transfer.fetchArticle.optimizeHint: A fetched article’s body has no layout styling at all — leave this unchecked and it renders on the device with default paragraph spacing, leaving large blank gaps. Checking it runs a "clean + optimize" pass immediately after fetching (the same thing as clicking "Optimize" in the master library list, just done for you). Uncheck it if you want the rawest possible result — e.g. to decide later yourself whether to optimize it.

manage.lab.comicMargin.title: Comic page margin: minimal
manage.lab.comicMargin.desc: Only affects comic EPUBs (mostly images; text pages such as a copyright page are fine; text books and PDFs are untouched). When on: (1) comic pages you optimize afterwards are padded to a wider page frame, and pure-text pages (copyright, recap, chapter titles) get side margins automatically; (2) after a comic is added to xochitl, the reader sets its page margin to 1 (almost zero) the first time you open that book — images grow from about 260pt to about 302pt wide (page width 303pt) and the side whitespace drops from 20/23pt to about 0. It uses the reader's own page-margin setting rather than editing files, so changing it back in "Text settings" afterwards sticks. Only applies to comics optimized and added after you turn it on; comics already on the device must be re-optimized from the original file and added again. New feature, off by default. See bookconv whitepaper §20.

manage.enhance.pageTurn.desc: Both switches only affect xochitl's built-in reader and are off by default; they are read when a book is opened, so reopen the book after changing them.
manage.enhance.pageTurn.tapHint: Tap the left or right edge (about 7% wide, 45%–80% of the screen height) to turn pages: right edge = next, left edge = previous. Elsewhere taps work as usual (double-tap for text, links).
manage.enhance.pageTurn.rtlHint: For books whose EPUB declares right-to-left reading (common for manga), swiping left-to-right and tapping the left edge go to the next page. Other books are unaffected.

health.lead: A read-only check-up: data is collected only when you open this screen or press Refresh, never sampled in the background. Tap a badge for details.
health.deletedTitle: xochitl is still running the old copy of these extensions (marked (deleted) in its memory map). The new files take effect after a device reboot; don't restart xochitl on its own (it may crash while exiting)

health.fw.unknownTitle: The sha256 of /usr/bin/xochitl is not in packaging/firmware-allowlist.txt as built into the gateway: the firmware may have just been updated, or the suite was installed on new firmware with --force
health.servicesHint: "Up at … after boot" is when the service last became active; the duration includes pre-start steps. If a service was restarted after boot, these numbers are for that restart.
health.restartsTitle: How many times systemd has restarted this service since boot
health.prevBoot: Last 20 log lines from the previous boot
health.prevBootNone: Not available: the device journal is not persistent (kept in memory only), so the previous boot's log is gone after a restart.

cleanup.lib.title: Books in the xochitl library
cleanup.lib.desc: Old duplicate copies (such as the per-volume Naruto parts sent earlier) cannot be identified reliably, so nothing is picked automatically. The library's EPUBs and PDFs are listed for you to check (notebooks are not listed). Ticked books go through xochitl's own Move to Trash and can be restored from the xochitl trash; the gateway never deletes library files directly.
